# Conversion

Turn values into text, and text back into numbers, dates, booleans and JSON.

**Library:** [Standard library](index.md#standard-library), for apps and code-pipeline hooks. More in [Cogniscript](../../../concepts/cogniscript.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`BoolToString`](#booltostring) | Converts a bool to the text `true` or `false`, always in lower case. |
| [`DateTimeToString`](#datetimetostring) | Formats a date as text, in ISO 8601 form unless you give a format. |
| [`DecimalToString`](#decimaltostring) | Formats a decimal number as text, with `.` as the decimal point. |
| [`IntToString`](#inttostring) | Converts a whole number to text, such as `42` or `-7`. |
| [`JsonArrayToString`](#jsonarraytostring) | Writes a JSON array as text, either compact on one line or indented over several. |
| [`JsonObjectToString`](#jsonobjecttostring) | Writes a JSON object as text, either compact on one line or indented over several. |
| [`NumberToString`](#numbertostring) | Formats a number as text, writing a whole number without decimal places. |
| [`StringToBool`](#stringtobool) | Reads a bool from text. |
| [`StringToDateTime`](#stringtodatetime) | Reads a date from text, in any common form or in the exact format you give. |
| [`StringToDecimal`](#stringtodecimal) | Reads a decimal number from text, such as `3.14`, `-0.5` or `1e3`. |
| [`StringToInt`](#stringtoint) | Reads a whole number from text, such as `42` or `-7`. |
| [`StringToJsonArray`](#stringtojsonarray) | Checks that text is a JSON array and returns it, ready to store in a `jsonArray`. |
| [`StringToJsonObject`](#stringtojsonobject) | Checks that text is a JSON object and returns it, ready to store in a `jsonObject`. |

### BoolToString

Converts a bool to the text `true` or `false`, always in lower case.

```c
string BoolToString(bool value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `bool` | The bool to convert. |

**Returns** `string`: `true` or `false`.

Every value is held as text, and a bool's text varies: a `true` literal, a comparison and a system call that returns a bool all give `True` or `False`, while a bool read from JSON gives `true` or `false`. Use this call when the exact text matters, for example in output or in JSON you build as text.

Raises an error when `value` is not `true` or `false` (in any case). It does not accept `yes` or `1`; [`StringToBool`](#stringtobool) does.

### DateTimeToString

Formats a date as text, in ISO 8601 form unless you give a format.

```c
string DateTimeToString(date value, string format)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `date` | The date to format. Text such as `2026-11-02` works too. |
| `format` | `string`, can be empty | A .NET date format, such as `yyyy-MM-dd` or `dd MMM yyyy HH:mm`. Optional: pass `""` for ISO 8601. |

**Returns** `string`: The date as text.

With no format the result looks like `2026-11-02T14:30:05.0000000`. A value stored in a `date` variable keeps whole seconds and no time zone, so the fraction is zeros and the result never ends in `Z`, even for a time from [`DateGetUtc`](dates.md#dategetutc), which is UTC. Write the zone into the format if you need it: `DateTimeToString(now, "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ")`.

Formats use the invariant culture: English month and day names (`dddd d MMMM yyyy` gives `Monday 2 November 2026`) and the 24-hour clock with `HH`. A one-letter format must be one of the standard .NET date formats (such as `d`, `s` or `u`); any other letter raises `Input string was not in a correct format.`

### DecimalToString

Formats a decimal number as text, with `.` as the decimal point.

```c
string DecimalToString(decimal value, string format)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `decimal` | The number to format. |
| `format` | `string`, can be empty | A .NET number format, such as `F2` (two decimal places), `N2` (thousands separators and two decimal places) or `0.000`. Optional: pass `""` to write the number as it is. |

**Returns** `string`: The number as text.

With no format the number keeps the decimal places it has: `2.50` stays `2.50` and `3.0` stays `3.0`. [`NumberToString`](#numbertostring) is the same except that it writes a whole number such as `3.0` as `3`. Formats use the invariant culture, so `N2` writes `1234.5` as `1,234.50`.

### IntToString

Converts a whole number to text, such as `42` or `-7`.

```c
string IntToString(int value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `int` | The whole number to convert. |

**Returns** `string`: The number as text.

Raises an error when `value` is not a whole number between -2,147,483,648 and 2,147,483,647. A decimal is refused even when it is whole, such as `3.0`; use [`NumberToString`](#numbertostring) for decimals.

### JsonArrayToString

Writes a JSON array as text, either compact on one line or indented over several.

```c
string JsonArrayToString(jsonArray value, bool pretty)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `jsonArray` | The array to write. |
| `pretty` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` to indent the JSON; `false` or `""` for compact JSON on one line. |

**Returns** `string`: The array as JSON text.

Characters such as accented letters, an em dash or Arabic are written as they are, not as `\u` escapes. An empty value counts as an empty array and gives `[]`. Raises an error when `value` is not a JSON array.

### JsonObjectToString

Writes a JSON object as text, either compact on one line or indented over several.

```c
string JsonObjectToString(jsonObject value, bool pretty)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `jsonObject` | The object to write. |
| `pretty` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` to indent the JSON; `false` or `""` for compact JSON on one line. |

**Returns** `string`: The object as JSON text.

Characters such as accented letters, an em dash or Arabic are written as they are, not as `\u` escapes. Raises an error when `value` is empty or not a JSON object.

### NumberToString

Formats a number as text, writing a whole number without decimal places.

```c
string NumberToString(decimal value, string format)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `decimal` | The number to format. |
| `format` | `string`, can be empty | A .NET number format, such as `F2` or `N0`. Optional: pass `""` to write the number as it is, without decimal places when it is whole. |

**Returns** `string`: The number as text.

With no format, `3.0` gives `3` and `2.50` gives `2.50`. With a format it is the same as [`DecimalToString`](#decimaltostring). Formats use the invariant culture, with `.` as the decimal point. Without a format, a whole number larger than 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 (or smaller than its negative) raises an error.

### StringToBool

Reads a bool from text. Accepts `true` and `false`, and also `1` and `0`, `yes` and `no`, `y` and `n`, and `on` and `off`, in any case.

```c
bool StringToBool(string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to read. |

**Returns** `bool`: `true` or `false`.

Raises `Cannot convert 'maybe' to boolean` for any other text, including empty text.

### StringToDateTime

Reads a date from text, in any common form or in the exact format you give.

```c
date StringToDateTime(string value, string format)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to read. |
| `format` | `string`, can be empty | The exact .NET date format the text is in, such as `dd/MM/yyyy` or `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. Optional: pass `""` to accept any common form. |

**Returns** `date`: The date.

Without a format it accepts the forms the invariant culture knows, such as `2026-11-02`, `2026-11-02 14:30`, `2026-11-02T14:30:00Z` and `11/02/2026`. A date with slashes is read month first, so `02/11/2026` is 11 February; give a format such as `dd/MM/yyyy` for day-first dates.

A time zone or offset in the text (`Z`, `+02:00`) is converted to the server's local time, which is UTC. A stored `date` keeps whole seconds, so any fraction of a second is lost once you assign the result to a variable.

Raises `Cannot convert 'nope' to DateTime` when the text is not a date, and `Cannot convert '2026-01-02' to DateTime using format 'dd/MM/yyyy'` when it does not match the format.

### StringToDecimal

Reads a decimal number from text, such as `3.14`, `-0.5` or `1e3`.

```c
decimal StringToDecimal(string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to read. |

**Returns** `decimal`: The number.

The decimal point is `.`. A comma is read as a thousands separator, so `1,234.5` is 1234.5 and `1,5` is 15, not 1.5. It also accepts surrounding spaces, a sign before or after the number, and an exponent (`1e3` is 1000). Raises `Cannot convert 'abc' to decimal` for anything else, including empty text.

[`TypeIsDecimal`](type-checks.md#typeisdecimal) is stricter: it says `false` for an exponent such as `1e3`, which this call accepts.

### StringToInt

Reads a whole number from text, such as `42` or `-7`.

```c
int StringToInt(string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to read. |

**Returns** `int`: The number.

Spaces around the number, a leading `+` or `-` and leading zeros are allowed. Raises `Cannot convert 'abc' to integer` for anything else: empty text, a decimal point (even in `3.0`), a thousands separator, or a number outside -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647.

### StringToJsonArray

Checks that text is a JSON array and returns it, ready to store in a `jsonArray`.

```c
jsonArray StringToJsonArray(string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to check. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: The same text, as a JSON array.

The text comes back exactly as it was, not reformatted. Use it to fail early, with a clear message, on text you did not create, such as a model's answer. Raises `Value is not a JSON array, it is a Object` (or `String`, `Number`, and so on) when the text is JSON of another kind, and `Cannot parse '…' as JSON: …` when it is not JSON at all, including empty text.

### StringToJsonObject

Checks that text is a JSON object and returns it, ready to store in a `jsonObject`.

```c
jsonObject StringToJsonObject(string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to check. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The same text, as a JSON object.

The text comes back exactly as it was, not reformatted. Use it to fail early, with a clear message, on text you did not create, such as a model's answer. Raises `Value is not a JSON object, it is a Array` (or `String`, `Number`, and so on) when the text is JSON of another kind, and `Cannot parse '…' as JSON: …` when it is not JSON at all, including empty text.
